title: Case J — 1:1:2 building, non-isothermal
summary: Isolated 1:1:2 building with a floor tracer source in an unstably stratified boundary layer: velocity, temperature, tracer concentration and their turbulent fluxes at 444 points on three planes.

configuration.building: 1:1:2 (width : depth : height) prism, b = 0.08 m, H = 2b = 0.16 m
configuration.stratification: unstable: heated floor 45.8 degC, air at z = H 12.2 degC (difference 33.6 K), bulk Richardson number -0.086; building surface 22.0 .. 28.9 degC (mean 24.5 degC, 121 points in clean/cases/J/surface_temperature.csv)
configuration.source: 5 mm floor outlet at (0.04, 0, 0), 0.25 H beyond the leeward wall; 5 % ethylene in air at 30.4 degC, 9.17e-6 m3/s
configuration.concentration_normalisation: c0 = 0.05 q / (U_H H^2) = 12.283 ppm (the workbook's value; the 5 % gas fraction is in it)
configuration.instrument: split-fibre hot wire (velocity), cold wire (temperature), high-speed hydrocarbon analyser (concentration), 1000 Hz, 120 s per point
configuration.tunnel: thermally stratified wind tunnel, Tokyo Polytechnic University (Atsugi); 1.2 m wide, 1.0 m high
configuration.scale_note: model scale; the sources state no model:full scale ratio

units.temperature: degC (T); K (T_rms); heat fluxes K m/s

frame.origin: the building's leeward (downwind) wall centre on the ground; x = 0 is the leeward wall
frame.x: +x streamwise (the wind blows toward +x); the building spans x in [-0.08, 0]; the floor source is at x = +0.04
frame.y: +y lateral; the building spans y in [-0.04, 0.04]; the z/H = 0.025 plane is measured on the y <= 0 side only
frame.z: +z up; roof at z = 0.16; heated floor at z = 0

inflow_fit.method: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 2H on AF_caseJ.csv
inflow_fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ; the boundary layer is unstably stratified, so a neutral log law is only a rough description

known_issues: Temperature is in KELVIN in all three published CSVs; the API serves degrees Celsius (T) and kelvin differences (T_rms, heat fluxes).

The published CSV is the legacy workbook's non-dimensional values rounded to 3-4 decimals and scaled back; the table is rebuilt from the workbook. The CSV's heat fluxes sit on a 0.0049 K m/s grid and k on 0.00021 m^2/s^2.
c0 = 12.283 ppm includes the 5 % ethylene fraction of the released gas (workbook cell Co); q / (U_H H^2) alone is 245.7 ppm. The data paper states no c0 for Case J.
RS_caseJ.csv lists the location (-0.16, 0, 0.004) twice (No. 1 and 153, identical values): a score over the table counts that point twice.
The workbook's <u'2> is not always the square of its sigma_u (up to 3 % in single rows); the table uses the variances, which reproduce k.

The workbook lists an expanded uncertainty beside every quantity (no column here; clean/manifest.json cases.J.extra_measurements.expanded_uncertainty). The mean concentration is below its own uncertainty (about 1 ppm) at 42 % of the rows, and 193 uncertainty cells of the w'theta' flux are an Excel fill series, not values.

The empty-tunnel profile changes along the tunnel: U at z = 0.019 H is 0.33 U_H at x/H = -2.5 (the published AF_caseJ.csv), 0.58 at the building's own position. The workbook has all three stations (clean/cases/J/approach_flow_full.csv).
The readme's Reynolds number (43,000) is Case H's; U_H H / nu = 1.6e4 as the data paper states.
uv, uw, vw are not published at the points; uc, vc, wc were not measured.
citation_requested: Yoshie, R. (2016). Wind Tunnel Experiment and Large Eddy Simulation of Pollutant/Thermal Dispersion in Non-isothermal Turbulent Boundary Layer. Adv Environ Wind Eng, 167-196. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-4-431-55912-2_9
